findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_url_as_markdown, check_url_status, get_native_token_price · Private data: read_url_as_markdown, get_native_token_price · Public sink: compare_gas_costs.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_url_as_markdown, check_url_status, get_native_token_price · Private data: read_url_as_markdown, get_native_token_price · Public sink: compare_gas_costs

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_gas_price" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Current gas and fee prices for one chain. Current gas and fee prices for Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon or Solana: slow/standard/fast tiers and the USD cost of a transfer, USDC transfer and swap. Updated every 15 seconds. Paid via x402: the first call returns 402 with payment requiremen" → after: "Current gas/fee tiers and USD costs for one chain. Slow/standard/fast gas tiers and USD cost of a transfer, USDC transfer and swap, for Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon or Solana. Updated every 15s. Solana is compute-unit pricing, not gwei-style gas; the other 5 are EVM. Use for one chain"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
